name: San Marcial hermitage & the Battle of Irun
story: Mola's Navarrese columns under Colonel Alfonso Beorlegui attacked Irun to cut the Republican north off from France. Their attack was supported by German and Italian aircraft and a few light tanks. Basque militia, CNT units, Asturian miners and some French communist volunteers held the Puntza ridge and the San Marcial hill with its hermitage. France had closed the border, and the defenders ran short of ammunition. San Marcial fell after heavy fighting, and Irun was abandoned on 5 September. Retreating anarchists set parts of the town on fire. Beorlegui was wounded entering the town and later died. The Nationalist victory cut Gipuzkoa, Biscay, Santander and Asturias off from the French border.
see: The San Marcial hermitage on its hilltop, a good viewpoint over the 1936 battlefield, Irun, Hendaye and the Bidasoa. The pin marks the hermitage, not a firing position; the fighting positions are not signposted.
plan: A minor road and footpaths lead up from Irun to the hermitage (about 1 h on foot). The view is best on a clear day.
